items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: He says, "I'm here with the Goldkette band, you remember me," and I said, "Oh, sure." He said, "Well, how would you like to join the band?

ctx.x: I am pretty sure it was one of those semi-classic tunes. Anyway, I said okay. I had time and I made them an arrangement of "Blue Room." At that time, I dumped everything in it. At that time I had used before, what they call a buildup, chord, I hadn't heard anybody else use it. You know, this start on one note, and go through the whole scale. (Sings) and I stuck it in there and oh, boy, they took it. They liked it.

But anyway, I am getting ready to go and it can't be more than four or five days now that I get a telephone call and it's from Ludwig. They're up in a place in Massachusetts, Southboro, Massachusetts. He says, "I'm here with the Goldkette band, you remember me," and I said, "Oh, sure." He said, "Well, how would you like to join the band? Oh, boy. Well, I am going away to school. You would like me to make some arrangements?" and I said, "What will I do with my horn?" and he said "Bring it along."
I had then a baritone, a bass clarinet, if you look at any of those early pictures, everybody played those things.
